file_name: Poot et al. - 2023 - The Design of a Persuasive Game to Motivate People with Asthma in Adherence to Their Maintenance Med.txt

barriers.description: The study had a small number of participants per design phase, limiting the breadth of user input available to the design team.
barriers.justification: Limited participant numbers constrained the designers' ability to manage user understanding and to thoroughly evaluate and iterate prototypes across diverse user needs.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Second, the small number of participants per design phase may have an influence on the study findings.

barriers.description: The user-testing period was very short (five days), preventing assessment of long-term engagement and effects.
barriers.justification: The short testing duration hindered the designers' ability to evaluate long-term usage and to integrate iterative feedback about sustained engagement and adherence.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Finally, the limited duration of the testing period (ie, five days) calls for caution in drawing conclusions regarding long-term usage.

barriers.description: Not all components of the Ademgenoot game were included in the formative evaluation.
barriers.justification: Incomplete component testing limited the designers' capacity to fully evaluate the prototype and to iterate on all parts of the system based on user feedback.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Third, the formative evaluation of Ademgenoot may also present some limitations as not all components of the Ademgenoot game were tested.

barriers.description: Participants were relatively young, which may have limited representativeness of findings.
barriers.justification: A skewed age sample constrained designers' ability to manage user understanding and specify requirements for older or more diverse populations, limiting generalizability of design decisions.
barriers.reference_excerpt: First, the relatively young participants could have limited the representativeness of our findings and the applicability of the Ademgenoot concept.

barriers.description: Researcher interference may have altered participant behavior during testing (observer effect).
barriers.justification: Behavior change caused by observation undermines the designers' ability to accurately evaluate natural user interactions and to integrate authentic feedback into iteration cycles.
barriers.reference_excerpt: In addition, interference by the researcher may have led to changes in behavior (ie, improved medication adherence) due to the individual being observed.

barriers.description: The study focused only on individuals with mild asthma, limiting applicability to other patient groups.
barriers.justification: This narrow focus restricted designers' ability to address holistic experiences and specify requirements for users with differing severity, thus constraining design generalizability and future iterations.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Finally, the focus of our study on individuals with mild asthma may limit the generalizability of our findings to other patient groups.

barriers.description: Commercial feasibility concerns were raised for some inhaler use patterns (eg, Symbicort SMART), creating uncertainty about market alignment.
barriers.justification: Stakeholder commercial constraints limited designers' ability to define technically and commercially viable requirements and could restrict design solutions or deployment options.
barriers.reference_excerpt: However, as some patients receive Symbicort as Symbicort Maintenance and Reliever Therapy (SMART), the commercial feasibility (ie, complementing business strategies) may be less clearly defined.

barriers.description: Electronic dose-monitoring (EDM) systems have limited large-scale implementation due to lack of long-term evidence and disengagement issues with existing apps.
barriers.justification: These systemic stakeholder-level barriers constrain designers' ability to implement and evaluate the intervention in real-world settings and to produce and test solutions at scale.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Despite its potential, EMDs have not yet been implemented on a large scale in practice due to, amongst others, the need for evidence on long-term effectiveness and disengagement challenges with existing apps.

barriers.description: Integration requirements with existing inhalers and electronic health records (EHRs) pose implementation constraints.
barriers.justification: External technical and organizational integration needs limit designers' ability to produce deployable solutions and may restrict design choices or require additional stakeholder coordination.
barriers.reference_excerpt: This requires EMD programs to be compatible with existing inhalers preferably integrated within existing electronic health records.
